name: 1st Red Bull Air & Style
description: Inaugural edition, a single straight jump with a USD 10,000 purse. Organisers expected about 100 spectators and over a thousand came. Some sources (World Snowboard Federation, Collective) date the event's founding to 1993; the contest itself is dated 17 January 1994 by Wikipedia and Austria-Forum.

description: Second edition held in the same calendar year as the first, after the contest moved to a December date; belongs to the 1994/95 season.

name: 7th G-Shock Air & Style
description: Over 45,000 spectators. A crowd crush as the venue emptied after the show killed five people; a sixth, one of five badly injured teenagers, died four years later of the consequences. A court found that Tyrol and the city of Innsbruck should have cancelled the event because the venue was unsafe. Innsbruck refused permission for further events and the contest moved to Seefeld.

name: 8th G-Shock Air & Style
description: First edition after the move from Innsbruck to Seefeld, under a five-year contract.

name: 9th Nokia Air & Style

name: 12th Nokia Air & Style
description: Last Seefeld edition before the move to Munich.

name: 13th Nokia Air & Style
description: First Munich edition.

name: 14th Nokia Air & Style

name: 1st Billabong Air & Style quarterpipe, Innsbruck
description: Air & Style returned to the Bergisel with a quarterpipe format, numbered separately from the big air series.

name: 16th Air & Style, Munich

name: 2nd Billabong Air & Style quarterpipe, Innsbruck

name: 17th Billabong Air & Style, Innsbruck
description: Whitelines records Marko Grilc winning with a double cork.

name: 18th Air & Style, Beijing

name: 20th Nike 6.0 Air & Style, Munich

name: 23rd Air & Style, Beijing

name: 24th Billabong Air & Style, Innsbruck

name: Air & Style Mexico City

name: 25th Air & Style, Beijing

name: Air + Style Beijing 2014
description: Opening stop of the three-city 2014/15 Air + Style tour, the first season with Shaun White as majority owner.

name: Air + Style Innsbruck 2015

name: Air + Style Los Angeles 2015
description: First Air + Style in North America and the finale of the 2014/15 tour, built on a 16-storey scaffold with a 70 ft jump.

name: Air + Style Beijing 2015

name: Opel Air + Style Innsbruck 2016
description: First year at Olympiaworld rather than in the Bergisel stadium (Onboard's report places the arena in an open car park beside the Bergisel). Strong valley winds forced organisers to cancel the rounds after round two and to score the podium from the three highest combined round-two scores. Collective reports 2016 as the first year women competed at Innsbruck; Method Mag says the first women's field at Innsbruck was 2017. Shaun White announced during the event that the tour would expand to five stops. Exact dates not found in a source I opened.

name: Air + Style Los Angeles 2016
description: Second LA edition, moved from the Rose Bowl to Exposition Park next to the LA Coliseum; 16-storey big air jump plus two music stages.

name: Air + Style Innsbruck-Tirol 2017
description: Method Mag calls this the 34th edition and says it was the first year women competed in the Air + Style big air, with 30 men and 8 women plus 16 live music acts over two days. Tiroler Tageszeitung reports the Air+Style contest's history ended in 2017 in the Olympiaworld car park. Edition numbering here (34th) is inconsistent with Wikipedia's numbering (25th for Beijing 2013).

name: Air + Style Beijing 2017

name: Argentina Snowboard Tour 2012
description: Five events between May and August 2012: urban big airs in Buenos Aires (one of them invitational) plus stops at Cerro Chapelco, Cerro Bayo and Cerro Catedral. All but the invitational open to any rider regardless of nationality or level.

name: Argentina Snowboard Tour 2014
description: Third tour stop was the Snow Travel South America Snowboard Challenge slopestyle at La Hoya on 20 August 2014, the second time La Hoya hosted it and the final stop of the season for Brazilian riders. Other 2014 stops not listed in the source. Related Argentine events reported the same season: Rip Curl Grom Winter Search and the ALIVE and KICKING Rip Curl Pro (23 Aug) at Cerro Catedral, Bariloche, and the DC Slopestyle Pro at Cerro Chapelco (5 Aug).

name: Nine Knights & Nine Queens 2014

name: Audi Nines 2018

name: Audi Snowboard Series 2013/14
description: More than 30 events across Switzerland in freestyle, boardercross and race. Named stops include a 3-Star World Snowboard Tour contest at Laax and European Cups at Davos, Lenzerheide and Lenk; the Swiss Championships in all three disciplines close the season, with the freestyle championships at Corvatsch on 11-12 April 2014.

Note that later edition numbering used by the organisers and the World Snowboard Federation (2011 = 12th annual, 2012 = 13th annual) counts the first edition as 2000, so the year of this first edition is disputed.

name: 2001 Burton European Open
description: The only year alpine snowboarders competed alongside the freestyle disciplines.

description: The fourth 6Star stop of the Swatch TTR World Snowboard Tour season and the first event that season to host both men's and women's fields, with 1000 ranking points per discipline.

name: 12th Annual Burton European Open (2011)
description: Eight-day 6Star TTR event with over 300 riders and a USD 125,000 prize purse. Peetu Piiroinen and Kelly Clark won the halfpipe.

description: Men's, women's and junior fields in slopestyle and halfpipe. Points counted toward both the TTR and the Burton Global Open Series rankings. The only documented year the BEO ran in late February rather than January.

description: Presented by MINI. Halfpipe semi-finals on the LAAX superpipe 2014-01-16 with finals 2014-01-17; Iouri Podladtchikov and Ursina Haller won the halfpipe. Full event dates not sourced.
